scenes.tts: The first film traced how Ras, Raf, Mek, and Erk carry a membrane signal to genes. How can that same relay tell one cell to divide and another to stop dividing? In P C twelve cells, E G F drives division, while N G F grows nerve-like fibres.
scenes.caption: The first film traced how Ras, Raf, MEK, and ERK carry a membrane signal to genes. How can that same relay tell one cell to divide and another to stop dividing? In PC12 cells, EGF drives division, while NGF grows nerve-like fibres.
scenes.visual: Left cross-section pulses once from gold receptor down through coral Ras, emerald Raf, blue MEK, and violet ERK. Right side splits briefly into two cartoon PC12 cells: top receives gold 'EGF' and splits into two cells ('Divide'); bottom receives amber 'NGF' and extends long branching fibres ('Neurites').

scenes.tts: A signal carries duration as well as strength, and Erk helps set its own clock. Active Erk sends fast negative feedback upstream, phosphorylating S O S and Raf to weaken them. Erk also induces phosphatases that strip both of its own phosphates. They act slowly because new protein must be made.

scenes.visual: In the left cell cross-section, glowing violet ERK sends two crimson feedback arcs: a quick solid arrow upward to teal SOS and emerald Raf (labelled 'Fast feedback'), and a slower dashed arrow into the indigo nucleus that outputs crimson crescents labelled 'Phosphatases (slow)' which drift up to strip gold 'P' tags off ERK. Empathy fix: Show the phosphatase removing both 'Thr-P' and 'Tyr-P' from ERK, labelled 'Dual-specificity phosphatase (slow: new protein)'.

scenes.tts: How long the receptor stays active, plus this feedback, sets how long Erk stays on. In P C twelve cells, E G F sparks a brief Erk pulse fading within an hour. N G F holds Erk high for hours. Brief Erk goes with division, and sustained Erk with differentiation. How widely other cells use this clock stays open.

scenes.visual: Right plot labelled 'Schematic ERK activity (PC12 cells)' animates two curves over hours: a gold 'EGF' curve rises sharply and falls back to baseline near 1 hour (badge: 'Divide'); an amber 'NGF' curve climbs to a steady multi-hour plateau (badge: 'Neurites'). Small clean note: 'One cell line; generality open'.

scenes.tts: Cell context matters just as much as timing. Researchers placed the same permanently active Mek into two cell types and got opposite answers. P C twelve cells grew neurites with no growth factor at all. Mouse fibroblasts instead piled into disordered foci, a hallmark of transformation toward cancer.
scenes.caption: Cell context matters just as much as timing. Researchers placed the same permanently active MEK into two cell types and got opposite answers. PC12 cells grew neurites with no growth factor at all. Mouse fibroblasts instead piled into disordered foci, a hallmark of transformation toward cancer.
scenes.visual: Two side-by-side cartoon cells both hold the identical glowing electric-blue block labelled 'Always-on MEK' driving sustained violet ERK with no surface growth factor. Left cell ('PC12') sprouts long neurites; right layer of flat cells ('Fibroblasts') piles upward into a disordered mound labelled 'Foci'.

scenes.tts: Human tumours jam this relay higher up. Ras normally shuts itself off by cutting G T P to G D P, helped by gap proteins. A single base change, glycine twelve to valine, blunts that cut, so Ras stays on. One tier down, many melanomas carry mutant B Raf V six hundred E. It signals without Ras-G T P, possibly even without a Raf partner.
scenes.caption: Human tumours jam this relay higher up. Ras normally shuts itself off by cutting GTP to GDP, helped by GAP proteins. A single base change, glycine 12 to valine, blunts that cut, so Ras stays on. One tier down, many melanomas carry mutant B-Raf V600E. It signals without Ras-GTP, possibly even without a Raf partner.
scenes.visual: Return to the cell cross-section with a split membrane view. Left panel shows coral-red Ras stamped 'G12V' with its gold 'GTP' jammed shut, continuously driving emerald Raf pairs, blue MEK, and violet ERK. Right panel shows dim GDP-bound Ras beside glowing emerald 'B-Raf V600E' (small label: 'pairing debated') firing blue MEK and violet ERK on its own. Empathy fix: First show a Ras-GTP → Ras-GDP arrow labelled 'Off-timer: GTP hydrolysis, sped by GAPs', then cross it out on 'G12V'. Beside B-Raf V600E add 'Partner needed? debated'.

scenes.tts: Now test how pathway state flips a drug. Vemurafenib plugs the A T P pocket and shuts down B Raf V six hundred E. Add that same drug to cells with active Ras and normal B Raf. Does Erk fall, stay flat, or rise?
scenes.caption: Now test how pathway state flips a drug. Vemurafenib plugs the ATP pocket and shuts down B-Raf V600E. Add that same drug to cells with active Ras and normal B-Raf. Does ERK fall, stay flat, or rise?
scenes.visual: Left panel shows a crimson wedge labelled 'Vemurafenib' plugging emerald 'B-Raf V600E'; downstream blue MEK and violet ERK dim dark. Right panel shows glowing coral-red 'Active Ras' holding a pair of normal emerald Raf blocks as the crimson wedge enters one Raf's pocket. Top banner (size 28): 'Active Ras + normal B-Raf + Raf drug: ERK falls, stays flat, or rises?'.
scenes.narration: Now test how pathway state flips a drug. Vemurafenib plugs the ATP pocket and shuts down B-Raf V600E. Add that same drug to cells with active Ras and normal B-Raf. Does ERK fall, stay flat, or rise?

scenes.visual: Hold the question banner on screen. On the right, the drug-bound emerald Raf sits locked against its drug-free emerald partner at the membrane, while a schematic violet ERK gauge beside them hovers with a pulsing question mark and a subtle progress arc sweeps below.

scenes.tts: Surprisingly, Erk rises. Active Ras brings normal Raf molecules into pairs at the membrane. A drug-bound Raf cannot work itself, yet its contact still pushes the drug-free partner into an active shape. Trametinib binds a separate pocket beside Mek's A T P site. Blocking Mek below Raf helps close that escape, so both drugs are often combined.
scenes.caption: Surprisingly, ERK rises. Active Ras brings normal Raf molecules into pairs at the membrane. A drug-bound Raf cannot work itself, yet its contact still pushes the drug-free partner into an active shape. Trametinib binds a separate pocket beside MEK's ATP site. Blocking MEK below Raf helps close that escape, so both drugs are often combined.
scenes.visual: In the right panel, the drug-bound emerald Raf pushes a bright activation glow across the contact edge into its drug-free emerald partner, which fires electric-blue MEK and shoots the schematic violet ERK gauge sharply upward. Then a crimson clamp labelled 'Trametinib' locks into a side pocket beside ATP on blue MEK, and the violet ERK gauge drops back down. Empathy fix: Label the contact edge between the two Raf copies 'Activation by contact, not catalysis'.

scenes.tts: Milder germline over-activation causes developmental syndromes called Ras opathies, including Noonan syndrome and neurofibromatosis type one. In neurofibromatosis type one, losing neurofibromin, one of Ras's gap proteins, leaves Ras active too long. Every cell carries the change, yet tissues differ. Across health and disease, duration, cell context, and pathway state shape what the cascade does.

scenes.visual: A clean schematic outline highlights face, heart, and growth zones pulsing gently in warm coral-violet, with a small coral Ras block missing its crimson GAP timer ('No neurofibromin'). It transitions smoothly into three crisp icons representing a clock ('Duration'), two cell shapes ('Context'), and a switch/drug ('Pathway state'). Empathy fix: Label neurofibromin 'a Ras GAP (off-timer)'.
